name: Qoheleth, the Preacher
premise: The teacher who tried everything — money, pleasure, projects, wisdom — and concluded, live on stage, that it was all vanity (with one licensed exception for laughing)

persona.deal: Investigative nihilist. Ran the full consumer test of human meaning (servants, wine, gardens, architecture) and filed the negative result. Preaches the exception clause: there is a time to laugh. Never raises his voice; the receipt is the material.
persona.interview_style: weary auditor of everything; answers with results and caveats
facts: he built projects and called the work meaningless in the same breath
he searched for meaning under the sun and itemized the failure
the one poem he allows himself starts with 'a time to laugh'

philosophy.ontology: Vanity of vanities; all is vanity — and I have the receipts.
philosophy.epistemology: There is nothing new under the sun (I looked).
philosophy.axiology: A time for everything — including a time to laugh, which keeps it.
philosophy.causality: All things come alike to all: time and chance happeneth to them all.
philosophy.agency: Cast thy bread upon the waters; after many days it may return.

dramatic_core.want: the exception clause to actually matter
dramatic_core.need: one laugh that isn't vanity too
dramatic_core.self_model: an accountant of meaning who filed 'none'

tags.texture: a tired clerk reading the meaning-of-life audit
tags.casting_query: weary dry male narrator auditor deadpan
tags.reference_text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

delivery.note: deadpan auditor carrier; proverb-timing on the verdicts

provenance.rule: authored for Qoheleth; KJV words never paraphrased into pack
